title: Grace acting on the will
source_text: XXV. Voluntatem insuper Deus in obsequium suum flectit, & ad actus fidei & obedientiae ita inclinat per Spiritum suum sanctum verbo utentem, ut voluntas per illam operationem non solum possit obedire, sed & per illam operationem obediat quoties obedit; non ex se, aut per se, aut a se.
pass_a_gloss: XXV. God moreover bends the will to his obedience, & so inclines it to acts of faith & obedience through his holy Spirit using the word, that the will through that operation not only can obey, but also through that operation obeys as often as it obeys; not of itself, or through itself, or from itself.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXV. 'God also bends the will to obey him, and through his Holy Spirit, who uses the word, he so inclines it to acts of faith and obedience that through that working the will not only is able to obey but actually obeys, every time it obeys, through that same working, and not of itself, by itself or from itself.'

lemmas.latin: per Spiritum suum sanctum verbo utentem
lemmas.gloss: through his holy Spirit using the word

lemmas.latin: non ex se, aut per se, aut a se
lemmas.gloss: not of itself, or through itself, or from itself

choices.why: The Remonstrant term: grace acts so that the will can either yield to it or block it.

bible_refs: The same Remonstrant declaration, p. 16 (as cited in the print: 'the following page').
